reviewers.interpretation_notes: Read as the brief normalizes it. Every element of the Supported condition holds. (1) Standing limit: s.38(1) of Bylaw 18155: 'Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.' The last amendment noted under s.38 is S.15, Bylaw 20226, July 4, 2022. (2) The cut: under item 1.4, a motion moved by M. Janz says the committee will 'adjust the rules on time limits as set out in section 38 of Bylaw 18155' for the 2026-08-26 meeting so that 'each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes'. It carried 6 to 0. (3) Coverage: the motion's words reach 'each approved speaker' at the meeting. It is not limited to item 7.6 or to any class of speaker. (4) Primary count N = 64 (panels 15+15+15+15+4), inside 60-80. ALTERNATIVES (my calculations from the carried minutes, counting entries): (a) Alternative band 50-90 with N=64: Supported, so the row is unchanged. (b) N-all = 79, made up of item 7.1: 5; item 7.3: 1; item 7.4: 8 in the 2.3 motion plus 1 in the additional-speaker motion (4 to 0) = 9; item 7.6: 64. 79 is inside 60-80 and inside 50-90, so Supported under both, though 79 is one entry below the primary band's upper edge. A person approved on two items would appear twice in N-all, and the carried text cannot show whether anyone did. (c) N-spoke = 52 (presentation panels 16+16+18+2). That is outside the primary band 60-80, giving Partially supported (the count fails the magnitude rule while the 5-to-3 cut for every approved speaker holds). It is inside the alternative band 50-90, giving Supported. So the finding is DEFINITION-SENSITIVE: under N-spoke with the primary band the row changes from Supported to Partially supported. The story should say so beside the verdict. QUALIFICATIONS. Q1: The motion sits under item 1.4 (Adoption of Agenda), moved by M. Janz, and names section 38 of Bylaw 18155. Limits set: 3 minutes per approved speaker; for each member of Council, 3 minutes to ask questions and 3 minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion (standing limits 5 minutes each under s.38(5) and s.38(6)). In favour (6): E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack, A. Paquette. Opposed: none recorded. Carried 6 to 0. The motion does not cite s.4 or use the words 'special resolution'. Special resolution (s.2(2)(m)) needs at least two-thirds of all members of the Standing Committee. The minutes' header lists six members present, and roll call notes Mayor Knack is a member under s.15(3) of Bylaw 18156. My calculation: 2/3 x 6 = 4, and 6 in favour >= 4, so the requirement was met on the minutes' record. A larger membership of up to 9 would still be met. Q2: It applies to every approved speaker at the meeting, across all four items, not only item 7.6. Q3: In the minutes' order the motion is the third motion under item 1.4. It comes after the agenda-adoption and Orders of the Day motions, before the item 2.3 Requests to Speak motion, and before item 7.6. Item 2.4 made item 7.6 the first item of business, so the motion also comes before the first public speaker on 7.6. Q4: Item 2.3 for item 7.6 has 5 panels: P1 15 entries (2 with an organization: Edmonton Bike Coalition, YEG Bike Coalition); P2 15 (8: Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, YEG Bike Coalition, Paths for People, Ward Métis Bikes x3); P3 15 (3: Let's Bike There YEG, Bike Edmonton, YEG Bike Coalition); P4 15 (2: Paths for People, YEG Bike Coalition); P5 4 (0). N = 64, of which 15 entries carry an organization. By organization: YEG Bike Coalition 4, Ward Métis Bikes 3, Paths for People 2, and one each for Edmonton Bike Coalition, Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Let's Bike There YEG and Bike Edmonton. No further additional-speaker motion for 7.6 appears in the carried items. Q5: N-all by item: 7.1 = 5 (5 with organizations: Edmonton Construction Association x3, Big Lake Community League, PCL Construction Management Inc.); 7.3 = 1 (Alberta Avenue Business Association); 7.4 = 9 (8 + 1 additional; 6 with organizations: Alberta Ecotrust Foundation x2, Solar Alberta x2, Big Lake Community League, BILD Edmonton Metro); 7.6 = 64. Total 79. Q6: Presentations under 7.6, in 4 panels: P1 16 entries (5 with organizations: YEG Bike Coalition x2, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Paths for People); P2 16 (6: Bike Bus Alberta, Ward Métis Bikes x2, Let's Bike There YEG, Bike Edmonton, Paths for People); P3 18 (1: YEG Bike Coalition); P4 2 (0). N-spoke = 52, of which 12 entries carry an organization. Presentation panels are numbered and composed differently from the Requests to Speak panels. N = 64 and N-spoke = 52 are reported side by side; no difference is computed. Q7: The carried items record no speaker given more or less than the limit and no motion extending any speaker's time. 5 public-speaker attachments are listed under item 7.6 (attachment entries 11-15, labelled Panel 3, 2, 1, 4, 3; titles not reproduced). Q8: No City record stating a reason for the motion was identified (search described in limitations). Q9: No earlier meeting since 2025-10-29 adjusting s.38 was identified, but my search was not systematic (see limitations).

The primary count is 64 entries approved on item 7.6, within the specified 60–80 band. The committee's broader list covered other agenda items, and 52 entries are recorded as presenting on item 7.6. Using N-spoke instead of N changes the result to Partially supported under the primary band: the five-to-three-minute change is established, but 52 is below the band's lower bound. Under the alternative 50–90 band, N-spoke is within range and the result is Supported. N-all is 79 and remains Supported under both bands. The motion applied to each approved speaker at the meeting, not only speakers on item 7.6.

Supported under the primary measure: item 7.6 has 64 approved-speaker entries, within 60–80. The result also holds under the 50–90 band and using N-all (79). Using N-spoke (50) instead yields Partially supported under 60–80: the speaking-time reduction holds, but the specified queue magnitude fails. N-spoke yields Supported under 50–90. The finding is definition-sensitive because approved entries and presentations answer different questions. The motion changed a maximum; the minutes do not show that each speaker used three minutes.

round2_positions.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged from round 1. All three seats agree on the elements that decide the verdict: a 5-minute standing limit (s.38(1)), a carried 6–0 motion under item 1.4 setting a 3-minute maximum for each approved speaker at the meeting, and N = 64 entries on item 7.6, which is inside 60–80. I recounted the carried text entry by entry. N = 15+15+15+15+4 = 64, with 15 entries carrying an organization (2+8+3+2+0). N-all = 5 (item 7.1) + 1 (item 7.3) + 9 (item 7.4: 8 plus 1 additional speaker) + 64 (item 7.6) = 79; a person approved on two items would appear twice. N-spoke = 16+16+18+2 = 52, with 12 entries carrying an organization (5+6+1+0). Rows, primary band 60–80: N 64 Supported; N-all 79 Supported; N-spoke 52 Partially supported, because the cut is established but 52 is below the band. Rows, alternative band 50–90: N, N-all and N-spoke are all Supported. N-spoke changes the row under the primary band, so the finding is definition-sensitive. It holds for people approved to speak on the item and not, under the primary band, for people recorded as presenting. The motion is the committee's, not Council's. It applied to 'each approved speaker' at the meeting, on every item, not only item 7.6. It also cut members of Council to three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion, down from 5 minutes under s.38(5) and (6). It sets a maximum; the minutes do not record how long anyone actually spoke. The minutes record no reason for the motion, and this verdict establishes nothing about why it was moved, whether the people listed were complainants or where they came from, whether three minutes was enough, or which way any speaker argued.

Supported under the required primary measure: the bylaw sets a five-minute maximum, the committee carried a meeting-wide three-minute maximum for each approved speaker, and the item 7.6 approved-speaker list has 64 entries. The motion passed 6–0; the minutes list six committee members, so the recorded vote meets the bylaw's two-thirds-of-all-members threshold (two-thirds of six is four). Required alternatives: N=64 is Supported under the 50–90 band; N-all=79 is Supported under both bands; N-spoke=52 is Partially supported under the primary 60–80 band and Supported under the 50–90 band. The finding is definition-sensitive because using recorded presentations instead of approved entries changes the primary-band row. These are counts of entries, not verified distinct people. The motion set a maximum; the minutes do not establish how long any speaker actually spoke.

Supported under the brief's primary definitions: item 2.3 has 64 approved entries for item 7.6. The item 1.4 motion applies to every approved speaker at the meeting, not just item 7.6. Alternative results, holding other choices primary: N = 64 under the 50–90 band, Supported; N-all = 79 under either band, Supported; N-spoke = 52 under the 60–80 band, Partially supported, and under the 50–90 band, Supported. The finding is definition-sensitive because the presentation count changes the row under the primary band. The motion was the third under item 1.4, before Requests to Speak at item 2.3 and before the first item 7.6 speaker; item 2.4 designated 7.6 the first item of business. The minutes record a maximum, not each speaker's actual duration. They record no reason for the cut, speaker positions, or whether registrants were complainants. My round-1 presentation count was wrong; correcting it does not change the primary verdict or any alternative row.
